# Aurélien Nicosia

## Computational statistics, diagnostics and uncertainty

I hold a PhD in Statistics and a permanent teaching appointment at Université Laval. I develop methods for understanding latent states, directional data and atypical observations, connecting statistical methodology, R software and university teaching.

## Research, teaching and software

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-panel}
### A connected research program

Three themes: sequential model diagnostics, directional statistics and influence in density estimation. Methods are accompanied by simulation studies and reproducible materials.

[Contributions and directions](recherche.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::
::: {.feature-panel}
### Teaching and student training

Undergraduate and graduate teaching in French and English, student project advising and coordination of academic support through the CDA.

[Courses and supervision](enseignement.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::
::: {.feature-panel}
### Open software and resources

R packages on CRAN, software under development and teaching resources that make methods accessible and analyses verifiable.

[Software and documentation](packages.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::
:::

### Animal movement

An article is published in Methods in Ecology and Evolution, and two bioRxiv preprints focus on behavioural-state inference and sequential predictive diagnostics for hidden Markov models of animal movement.

::: {.link-list}
[MEE article](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.70313){.btn .btn-outline-dark}

### Recent packages on CRAN

`GLBFP`, `DonutMap`, `ggcircular`, `CircularRegression`, and `tutorizeR` support density estimation, statistical mapping, circular-data visualization, circular regression, and interactive tutorial creation.
